round1_closure_verification.implemented_in_code: mattel_news_source.py:445-450 — `if not isinstance(link, str) or not link.startswith(ARTICLE_URL_PREFIX): _notify(notifier, "Mattel article fetch error: invalid article link prefix"); return None`. The notifier message is a static literal that does NOT include `link`. The guard runs BEFORE `http.get` (line 454).

round1_closure_verification.finding: Round-1 #2 major ReDoS / regex correctness on _FLIGHT_PUSH_RE
round1_closure_verification.promised_in_spec: Decision 8 §2: linear-time character class `(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*`; no `(.+?)`; module-level compiled.
round1_closure_verification.implemented_in_code: mattel_news_source.py:54-56 — `_FLIGHT_PUSH_RE = re.compile(r'self\.__next_f\.push\(\[\s*1\s*,\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*\]\)')`. Linear-time character-class form, no lazy quantifier, module-level compile (single instance). MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE enforced before regex at line 396.

round1_closure_verification.finding: Round-1 #3 major json.loads RecursionError / depth not handled

round1_closure_verification.implemented_in_code: mattel_news_source.py:124-131 — js-string-unescape json.loads wrapped in `(json.JSONDecodeError, RecursionError, ValueError)`; mattel_news_source.py:197-202 — entries-array json.loads wrapped in same triple, raises MattelNewsError with type-name-only ES5 message. round1_closure_verification.finding: Round-1 #4 major bracket-match no termination / unbounded slice
round1_closure_verification.promised_in_spec: Decision 8 §4: depth-aware AND string-literal-aware bracket scanner with max-iter cap = len(unescaped); EOF without depth-zero → ES4. _resolve_body_html caps hex length at MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE.
round1_closure_verification.implemented_in_code: mattel_news_source.py:164-190 — bracket scanner tracks `depth`, `in_string`, `escape`; loop bound `while i < n` where `n = len(unescaped)`; on EOF without depth-zero raises ES4 (line 190). mattel_news_source.py:325-332 — `length = int(hex_len, 16)`; `if length < 0 or length > MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE: return ""` rejects huge advertised lengths BEFORE slice.

round1_closure_verification.finding: Round-1 #5 minor notifier info disclosure via raw str(exc)

MattelNewsError paths (lines 405-411, 472-478) use `str(exc)` only on our own exception class whose messages are constructed exclusively from safe scalars (`type(exc).__name__`, anchor names, byte sizes, validated slugs).

round1_closure_verification.finding: Round-1 #8 minor fixture-builder supply chain (placeholder defaults / accidental real-data leak)
round1_closure_verification.rationale: Round-2 closure left this finding open per security-review.json round1Closure[7].evidence: 'Decision 4 still describes builder purpose without mandating obviously-synthetic defaults... Re-raised below at minor severity.' However, code-level verification of the AS-BUILT builder (per task-03 checklist item 9) shows the implemented module has ZERO default URL values whatsoever — `_make_flight_listing(entries)` and `_make_flight_article(entry, body_html=None, body_chunks=1, truncate=False)` carry no default URL strings. All URL data flows through caller-supplied dicts. Module docstring (line 17-18) explicitly declares the placeholder convention (`example.com`, `placeholder.invalid`). Grep for `corporate.mattel.com|contentstack|hot-wheels-[a-z0-9]{3,}` in the builder returned zero matches. Therefore the residual minor finding is materially mitigated in code even though the round-2 spec did not explicitly close it. Recorded here for audit-trail; no code-level fail.

checklist.title: SSRF guard active (Decision 8 §1 / ES10)
checklist.evidence: mattel_news_source.py:445-450 — guard `if not isinstance(link, str) or not link.startswith(ARTICLE_URL_PREFIX): _notify(notifier, "Mattel article fetch error: invalid article link prefix"); return None` runs as the FIRST executable statement of `fetch_mattel_article` after the docstring (line 444). The notifier message is a static literal that does NOT include the `link` argument. `http.get` is line 454, AFTER the guard. No code path issues a request to `link` before validation.
checklist.comment: Notifier message has zero {link}/{exc} interpolation — purely static. Behavioural test in tests/test_mattel_news_source.py:570-589 verifies (a) returns None, (b) session.get not called, (c) notifier called once, (d) message contains 'invalid article link prefix' but NOT 'evil.example.com'.

checklist.title: Linear-time regex (Decision 8 §2)
checklist.evidence: mattel_news_source.py:54-56 — `_FLIGHT_PUSH_RE = re.compile(r'self\.__next_f\.push\(\[\s*1\s*,\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*\]\)')`. Character-class form `(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*` — no `.+?` lazy quantifier; correctly handles JS-escaped `\"`. Compiled once at module level (line 54), referenced via `_FLIGHT_PUSH_RE.findall(html)` at line 124.
checklist.comment: Single re.compile, never re-compiled inside hot path. Decision 8 §2 implementation verbatim.

checklist.title: JSON depth/recursion catch (Decision 8 §3)
checklist.evidence: Two json.loads call sites, both wrapped: (a) mattel_news_source.py:125-131 — `try: yield json.loads('"' + raw + '"') except (json.JSONDecodeError, RecursionError, ValueError): continue`; (b) mattel_news_source.py:197-202 — `try: decoded = json.loads(slice_text) except (json.JSONDecodeError, RecursionError, ValueError) as exc: raise MattelNewsError(f"invalid JSON in entries array: {type(exc).__name__}") from exc`. ES5 channel honored: type-name only, never raw exc.
checklist.comment: grep `json\.loads` returns exactly 2 matches at lines 129 and 198; both inside try/except with the required triple. No bare json.loads anywhere.

checklist.title: Bracket-match safety (Decision 8 §4 / ES4)
checklist.evidence: mattel_news_source.py:164-190 — `_find_entries_slice` tracks `depth=0`, `in_string=False`, `escape=False`. Inside-string state (line 172-178) handles `\\` escape via `escape=True` then consume; closing `"` flips `in_string=False`. Outside-string state (line 179-187) increments depth on `[`, decrements on `]`, returns when `depth==0`. Loop bound `while i < n` where `n = len(unescaped)` (line 167) — caps iterations at input length. EOF without depth-zero → `raise MattelNewsError("article2.entries not found")` at line 190 (ES4).
checklist.comment: No unbounded while-loop; cap is the input length itself. State-aware skip prevents bracket characters inside string literals (URLs containing `[` / `]`) from confusing depth tracking.

checklist.title: Hex-length cap (Decision 8 §4 / ES9c)
checklist.evidence: mattel_news_source.py:323-332 — `hex_len = match.group(1)`; `length = int(hex_len, 16)`; `if length < 0 or length > MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE: return ""`. Cap check runs BEFORE the slice at lines 334-340. `int("ffffffff", 16) = 4294967295 > 5*1024*1024` → returns `""` (content-empty path, no notifier per AC9). Negative guard (`length < 0`) is defence-in-depth — int(...,16) on non-negative hex is always >= 0, but the explicit check makes the contract clear.
checklist.comment: Adversarial `int("ffffffff",16)` (~4 GB) cannot trigger OOM slice; hex is also character-class-bounded by the surrounding regex `[0-9a-fA-F]+`.

checklist.title: Notifier sanitisation (Decision 8 §5)
checklist.evidence: RequestException paths (third-party exception class) — only type name: mattel_news_source.py:402-404 `f"Mattel news HTTP error: {type(exc).__name__}"`; mattel_news_source.py:467-470 `f"Mattel article fetch error ({link}): {type(exc).__name__}"`. MattelNewsError paths (our own exception, message constructed from safe scalars only) — lines 405-411, 472-478 use `str(exc)`; this is honored because every `raise MattelNewsError(...)` in the module passes only literals, anchor names, `type(exc).__name__`, validated digit slugs, or byte counts (verified via `grep raise MattelNewsError` across all 11 sites: lines 157, 162, 190, 200, 204, 221, 240, 282, 287, 397, 462). No `{exc}` / `{e}` / `repr(exc)` in any notifier-bound f-string (grep confirmed zero matches).
checklist.comment: Round-1 reviewer flagged ES6/ES7 `<link>` echo as minor info-disclosure but tech-spec explicitly accepts this trade-off (notes on rejected validator findings) since SSRF guard already validates link is a corporate.mattel.com URL. Recorded in additional_findings as severity=info.

checklist.title: `allow_redirects=False` (Decision 8 §6)
checklist.evidence: Listing path: mattel_news_source.py:388-393 — `http.get(url, headers={...}, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT, allow_redirects=False,  # Decision 8 control 6)`. Article path: mattel_news_source.py:454-459 — same kwarg list with `allow_redirects=False  # Decision 8 control 6`. Both call sites pass the kwarg explicitly.
checklist.comment: Regression-locked by tests at tests/test_mattel_news_source.py:319 and :550.

checklist.title: Log-suppression preserved (Decision 8 §6)
checklist.evidence: news_bot.py:184-185 — `for _noisy in ("httpx", "httpcore", "urllib3", "requests"): logging.getLogger(_noisy).setLevel(logging.WARNING)` intact (verified by reading lines 175-235). news_bot.py:226-228 — `logging.getLogger().addFilter(_TOKEN_FILTER); for _noisy in ("httpx", "httpcore", "urllib3", "requests"): logging.getLogger(_noisy).addFilter(_TOKEN_FILTER)` intact. mattel_news_source.py contains exactly one logging-related call: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` at line 36. No `logging.basicConfig`, no `setLevel(...)`, no `removeFilter`, no global mutation.
checklist.comment: Note: per task spec correction, log-suppression is implemented as module-level loops, NOT a `_configure_third_party_logging` function (that name does not exist in news_bot.py). Audit verifies the actual module-level loop infrastructure.

checklist.title: Builder placeholder-only defaults (round-2 minor #1, A06)
checklist.evidence: tests/fixtures/mattel_flight_builder.py — `_make_flight_listing(entries)` (line 53) and `_make_flight_article(entry, body_html=None, body_chunks=1, truncate=False)` (line 86) carry ZERO default URL string values. All URL/handle/title/thumbnail data flows through caller-supplied entry dicts. Module docstring (line 17-18) declares: 'All defaults use placeholder URLs (example.com, placeholder.invalid) so a stray test cannot accidentally surrogate a real Mattel/Contentstack URL.' grep `corporate\.mattel|contentstack|hot-wheels-[a-z0-9]{3,}` returned zero matches.
checklist.comment: Stronger than the AC requires: there are no default URLs at all; callers must explicitly construct entry dicts. No real Mattel data can be committed via builder defaults because there are no defaults.

checklist.title: TestSsrfGuard test coverage
checklist.evidence: tests/test_mattel_news_source.py:569-589 — `class TestSsrfGuard` with `test_rejects_link_outside_article_url_prefix`. Asserts: (a) `out is None`; (b) `session.get.assert_not_called()` (no HTTP issued); (c) `notifier.assert_called_once()`; (d) `'invalid article link prefix' in msg`; (e) `'evil.example.com' not in msg` — explicit malicious-URL non-leakage assertion.

additional_findings.category: A09:2021 Security Logging — link echo in ES6/ES7/ES9/ES9b
additional_findings.issue: Notifier messages for ES6/ES7 (mattel_news_source.py:469) and ES9/ES9b (mattel_news_source.py:477) echo the validated `link` argument back to admin chat in the format `Mattel article fetch error (<link>): <type>`. Tech-spec explicitly accepts this in 'Notes on rejected validator findings' (ACs section): SSRF guard ES10 runs FIRST so any link reaching this path is constrained to corporate.mattel.com, and echoing the path-only article slug helps the operator diagnose which article failed. Recorded for audit trail per task-03 spec edge-case guidance.
additional_findings.fix: Optional polish (NOT required by spec): truncate `link` to ~120 chars and/or strip query string before interpolation, e.g. `link.split('?', 1)[0][:120]`. The current behaviour is intentional per Decision 8 / tech-spec ACs notes and is contract-locked.

additional_findings.issue: _resolve_body_html compiles a fresh re.Pattern on every call (mattel_news_source.py:316-318). The `row_id` portion is sanitised via `re.escape` and constrained to `.isdigit()` (line 311), so this is not a ReDoS or injection vector — purely a micro-optimisation note carried over from round-1 security review.
additional_findings.fix: Optional: hoist a generic `(?:^|[^0-9])(\d+):T([0-9a-fA-F]+),` pattern compiled at module scope and post-filter group(1) == row_id; or wrap `_resolve_body_html` in `functools.lru_cache`. Pure performance polish; zero security impact.

summary: Approved. All 9 Decision-8 security ACs pass with explicit code evidence. All 4 round-1 security findings (1 critical SSRF + 3 major: ReDoS, JSON depth/recursion, bracket-match safety) closed and honored in code at the file:line level. Round-1 minor #8 (placeholder-defaults supply-chain) marked `not_addressed` in the tech-spec round-2 closure but is materially mitigated in the as-built builder (zero default URLs; all URL data flows from callers). OWASP A03/A05/A09/A10 sweep clean. Two informational findings recorded for audit trail: (1) ES6/ES7/ES9/ES9b link echo — tech-spec-accepted trade-off; (2) per-call regex compile in `_resolve_body_html` — performance polish, no security impact. No critical or major findings.
